description.value: The study compared subcortical structure volumes and vertex-wise surface morphology between alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls using 3T structural MRI, FSL, FIRST, and vertex analysis.

spans.text: We analyzed the volumes of 14 subcortical structures (bilateral thalamus, caudate, putamen, globus pallidus, hippocampus, amygdala, nucleus accumbens) in 21 alcohol-dependent subjects and 21 healthy controls using images acquired with 3T MRI.

description.value: Observational cross-sectional comparison of alcohol-dependent patients and age-matched healthy controls.

spans.text: Each alcohol-dependent subject was age-matched with a healthy control.

Vertex analysis was performed using FSL's generalized linear model to construct a statistical matrix and Randomize ( 16 ) to perform a non-parametric permutation inference on all the segmented subcortical structures.

value: Vertex analysis showed significant subcortical volumetric reductions in alcohol-dependent patients in the bilateral thalamus, bilateral putamen, right globus pallidus, right hippocampus, left caudate, and bilateral nucleus accumbens.
All significant reductions revealed by vertex analysis matched the volumetric reductions except in the left hippocampus and left caudate.

Thalamic reductions overlapped almost every defined thalamic substructure, while hippocampal reductions overlapped the presubiculum, hippocampal tail, hippocampal molecular layer, hippocampal fissure, fimbria, and CA3.

spans.text: Vertex analysis showed significant subcortical volumetric reductions of alcohol-dependent patients in the bilateral thalamus, bilateral putamen, right globus pallidus, right hippocampus, left caudate, and bilateral nucleus accumbens. All the significant reductions revealed from vertex analysis matched the volumetric reductions in all subcortical structures except in the left hippocampus and left caudate.
Figure 2A  shows each individual subcortical structure (light blue) overlaid on top of coronal, sagittal and axial MNI152 space, with yellow areas representing significant reductions.
